title: Means of the two slices
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $g:\{−1,1\}^{n+1}\to\{−1,1\}$ have uniform mean zero. For $b\in\{−1,1\}$, let $g_b$ be the restriction of $g$ to inputs whose first coordinate is $b$. Then the mean of $g_1$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at the singleton consisting of the first coordinate, and the mean of $g_{-1}$ is the negative of that coefficient.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a sign-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube
The uniform mean of $g$ is zero
